subject: Beryl Systems — Private Deployment onramp: networking & on-prem package
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@beryl.sys>, Procurement <procurement@beryl.sys>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Beryl Systems — Private deployment onramp: initial networking & on-prem checklist

Hi Alex / Beryl team,

Thanks for choosing Redwood for the private deployment. Per our kickoff call, I wanted to pull together the immediate networking and on-prem items so we have a single reference as we start the implementation sprint. Attached is a short checklist and a first-pass diagram from our side (see onprem-package-checklist.xlsx referenced).

Key asks from Redwood to Beryl before we lock the first-week deployment window:
- Confirm the three target subnets (CIDR blocks) you plan to peer with Redwood-managed VPCs and whether those subnets allow 443/TLS outbound to our NAT egress IPs.
- Share any proxy/firewall rules that will inspect or terminate TLS (we prefer TLS passthrough for token security).
- Provide short list of on-prem host OSes where the edge appliance will be installed (Linux distro + kernel version or Windows Server).
- Identify your network point-of-contact for configuration (name + phone).

Proposed next steps:
1) You share the inventory (beryl-network-inventory.xlsx) by EOD Wed 19 May.
2) We run a 45-minute network review with your infra lead; propose Thu 20 May or Fri 21 May.
3) Redwood delivers hardened on-prem package and installation runbook (we'll attach onprem-package-checklist.xlsx) and we agree on maintenance windows.

I'll coordinate calendar invites once you confirm availability. Monica is our implementation lead and Karthik will own the VPC peering config and routing policies.

Best,

Chloe Martin
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachment: onprem-package-checklist.xlsx (Excel)
From: Alex Greene <alex.greene@beryl.sys>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@beryl.sys>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Beryl Systems — Private deployment onramp: initial networking & on-prem checklist

Thanks Chloe — this looks good and actionable. A few clarifications from our side before the network review: 

On subnets and peering:
- We plan to peer three subnets: 10.10.128.0/24, 10.10.129.0/24, 10.10.200.0/24. Is there a required route propagation window we should expect on your end?

On private endpoints and DNS:
- Will Redwood publish private DNS names that resolve to the VPC endpoints, or do we need to create conditional forwarders to your resolver IPs?

On-prem package:
- Our infra team runs RHEL 8.7 (most hosts) and a small Windows Server 2019 fleet. Does your edge require any kernel modules or specific AMIs for virtualized installs?

Security/compliance:
- We will need a short list of audit logs you generate (connection logs, token lifecycle events) for our SOC review. Can you attach a sitemap of those logs?

I've attached our current network inventory (beryl-network-inventory.xlsx) and looped in Procurement for contract redlines.

If Thu 20 May 10:00 AM PT works for Redwood, that would be ideal.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Greene
Head of Cloud Ops | Beryl Systems
Attachments: beryl-network-inventory.xlsx (Excel)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@beryl.sys>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Procurement <procurement@beryl.sys>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Beryl Systems — Private deployment onramp: initial networking & on-prem checklist

Hi Alex — looping in the implementation team. Thanks for the inventory — that's exactly the level of detail we need. A couple quick notes before the network review: 

- Route propagation: on Redwood side we advertise routes within 2-5 minutes after peering is established; we do a controlled validation, so expect a short verification window.
- DNS: Redwood can publish private DNS records that resolve inside your VPC via conditional forwarding. We'll need the VPC resolver IPs (if you manage DNS) or we can provide a resolver endpoint as part of the private endpoint config.
- Kernel modules: for RHEL 8.7 we only require iptables/nftables standard networking stacks and the go-ldpreload helper for our edge agent; no custom kernel patches. Windows Server 2019 is supported via our installer but we recommend running the agent as a non-admin service under a dedicated account.

Proposed agenda for Thu 20 May 10:00 AM PT network review (45 min):
1) Introductions & roles (5 min)
2) Walkthrough of inventory & target subnets (10 min)
3) Peering, routing, and firewall rules (15 min)
4) On‑prem appliance install plan (10 min)
5) Next steps & owner assignments (5 min)

I've penciled the invite and will send a calendar once Alex confirms. Karthik will prepare the peering template and BGP/route table examples.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Mike Holton <mike.holton@networks-ops.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.inference>, Alex Greene <alex.greene@beryl.sys>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Beryl Systems — Private deployment onramp: initial networking & on-prem checklist

Hi all — Mike from Networks Ops here, supporting Beryl's infra team. A couple of tech questions for the upcoming review so we can be prepared: 

1) TLS inspection: if Beryl needs to keep TLS inspection on the path, are there certificate pinning options or a mutual TLS handshake we can use to avoid MITM issues?
2) NAT & egress IPs: please confirm the full list of Redwood egress IPs we should allow; if you plan changes during rollout, give a change window notice.
3) MTU/path MTU: our network has jumbo frames in the datacenter (9000 MTU). Any known issues with the edge appliance and larger MTUs?

I've attached a short note (edge-appliance-reqs.pdf) with our environment specifics. We prefer a short pre-check script from Redwood that validates connectivity and key ports prior to install — can you provide that?

Thanks,
Mike Holton
Senior Network Engineer (contractor)
Networks Ops
Attachment: edge-appliance-reqs.pdf (PDF)

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Beryl Systems — Private deployment onramp: initial networking & on-prem checklist — mutual action plan

Alex / Mike / Beryl team — thanks for the quick turn. Confirming outcomes and owners after the review and attachments we exchanged: 

Summary of decisions/actions:
- Subnets confirmed: 10.10.128.0/24, 10.10.129.0/24, 10.10.200.0/24 (owner: Beryl infra).
- Route propagation window: Redwood will advertise routes and validate within 2–5 minutes; Beryl to confirm acceptance by 21 May EOD.
- DNS: Redwood will publish private DNS entries and provide resolver IPs; Beryl to provide VPC resolver IPs in reply. (owner: Karthik / Beryl infra)
- On‑prem installs: RHEL 8.7 supported; Windows Server 2019 supported as service account install. We'll provide the pre-check script and the installer checklist. (owner: Monica)
- Security logs: Redwood will provide a short audit log manifest (connection attempts, token lifecycle events, install logs) by Tue 25 May for Beryl's SOC review.
- Change notice: Redwood will provide a 48-hour notice for any egress IP changes.

Deliverables (files and links):
- Redwood: network-diagrams_v1.pdf (attached) — internal topology and recommended firewall rules.
- Redwood: onprem-package-checklist.xlsx (attached) — install steps, service account requirements, rollback notes.
- Beryl: confirm VPC resolver IPs and accept route propagation by 21 May EOD.

Next meeting: Pilot install & smoke test — Tue 25 May 10:00 AM PT. Monica will send the invite and include the pre-check script.

If there are any outstanding blockers from Procurement (contract redlines), Procurement at Beryl and our legal team should escalate in the HubSpot thread (link above).

Thanks and looking forward to a smooth rollout.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: network-diagrams_v1.pdf (PDF), onprem-package-checklist.xlsx (Excel)
